messages:
elaine.sr: Hey team - customer asks if we can keep client source IP all the way through to their on-prem logging stack for a Private deployment. They want request-level attribution. Any blockers?
raj_se: Short answer: yes, but depends on the chosen egress pattern.
kevin_net: If they route via a NAT GW in their VPC we will lose original src IP. To preserve it we need one of:
- direct TLS passthrough to their onprem proxy (so we don’t terminate/proxy)
- preserve by using an L4 proxy that does TCP passthrough and preserves srcip
raj_se: For Redwood Private with an edge proxy, we typically terminate TLS at the customer edge or a customer-managed proxy so attribution lives in headers. They want "true" client IP in source field, not header.
mike_sales: Customer insists on source IP for their SIEM correlation. Are there any pricing or POC implications?
kevin_net: POC implication: we'll need to stand up a dedicated interface endpoint or a transit VPC tunnel with 1:1 NAT passthrough. That adds engineering time + infra cost. Estimate: 2-3 days for config + a small egress bandwidth bump during testing.
alice_sec: From a security/compliance view we prefer not to preserve raw client IP across shared infra. If customer is happy with Private deployment (VPC dedicated) we can allow it and lock to specific IPs. Need legal signoff for logging retention.
ajay@deploy-bot: deploy-bot: new env created: rdw-private-test-01 (private).
raj_se: Recommended architectures: 
1) Private dedicated (preferred): customer-managed edge proxy in their VPC that terminates TLS and forwards traffic to Redwood via PrivateLink with X-Forwarded-For preserved. Requires them to accept header-based attribution.
2) Transit VPC with GRE/IPSec: we peer the transit and we can preserve src IP via routed traffic. Works for onprem -> Redwood but requires cross-account routing and ACLs.
3) Direct peering (VPN/Direct Connect): preserves src IP end-to-end if they avoid NAT on their side, but we need documented firewall rules + routing.
mike_sales: Which of those is quickest for a 2-week POC?
kevin_net: Option 1 is fastest if they accept X-Forwarded-For. Option 2 is next but needs network team time. Option 3 depends on their DC/ISP lead time.
elaine.sr: They said they cannot rely on headers for attribution due to compliance. So option 2/3 only. Can you paste a minimal firewall/ACL checklist we can send to their network team?
kevin_net: Sure - paste below.
kevin_net: ```
# Minimal egress/ingress checklist for Transit/VPN path
- Allow outbound TCP 443 from customer-edge -> rdw-private-internal-ip-range (CIDR: 10.200.0.0/20)
- Allow inbound return traffic; ensure stateful flows allowed
- If using GRE/IPSec, allow protocol 50 (ESP) and UDP 500/4500 for IKE/NAT-T
- If using Direct Connect, set BGP neighbors and advertise customer prefixes
- No SNAT on the forwarding path to Redwood subnets (preserve src IP)
- Ensure MTU >= 1500 or adjust PMTU for GRE tunnels
- Whitelist specific Redwood egress IP block: 34.223.100.0/24 (example) and 52.12.200.0/24
```
raj_se: Add note: if on AWS Transit Gateway, attach a route table that sends customer prefixes to the Redwood attachment and set 'propagation' accordingly.
alice_sec: Also: logging & IDS must be enabled on their perimeter devices. Any retained client IPs must follow their retention PKI.
mike_sales: I'll forward this with an ask: timeline + whether they have a TAC ticket for Direct Connect.
elaine.sr: One more: do we need firewall exceptions for healthchecks / service discovery?
kevin_net: Health checks: allow outbound to these endpoints: `health.rdw-internal.example.com:8080` and `metrics.rdw-internal.example.com:9090`. If using PrivateLink, allow VPC endpoint interface ENI IPs.
raj_se: For POC we'll also add a fallback policy: if transit is down route via PrivateLink with header fallback so service remains available (but attribution drops). Document that as an SLA caveat.
mike_sales: Good call — I'll add to SOW: canary with header fallback + "preserved-src" mode during test window.
elaine.sr: Thanks all. Sharing with customer now. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rdw-private-test-01 provisioned (status: ready)
